description_good_justification: The README says in its first lines what tutor is: the AI side of the tutor of NovaTrail, an open platform for adaptive learning, interactive lessons and AI tutoring. It is a Go library that api, another component of the platform, calls in its own process: it reads the learner's work into an observation, reviews the working, assesses an essay against the module author's rubric and words the hints, and its eval runner is a command-line tool on the same code. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to obtain tutor (clone the repository with `git clone --recurse-submodules` and work in its devcontainer) and how to use what it has now, starting with `just board`. GitHub shows the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md on this repository's page, and they say how to give feedback and contribute: an issue first, then a pull request whose commits are signed off under the DCO, and a vulnerability reported privately. https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: Changes come as GitHub pull requests: an issue first, then a pull request whose every commit is signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin. The branch main takes changes only through pull requests whose required checks pass, and its ruleset has no bypass. The process is in the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md, which GitHub shows for this repository: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists what every contribution keeps to (no learners' data, no secrets, the devcontainer, licenses compatible with Apache-2.0, a DCO sign-off) and points to the rules every NovaTrail repository shares, RULES.md, which this repository's CLAUDE.md imports from spec at the tag it pins and which include the rule on tests: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/v0.9.4/RULES.md
floss_license_justification: Apache-2.0, an OSI-approved license, covers the code and the documents. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the OSI.
license_location_justification: The license is the top-level file LICENSE: https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README says what tutor is and how to use what it has now, each with its command: the check board (`just board`), which asks for the eval keys without showing them, its record mode (`just record`), the sheets that code draws, a measurement run and the report on its log. The Environment section of CLAUDE.md says how to start: clone with the spec submodule and open the repository in its devcontainer. RULES.md, which CLAUDE.md imports, says what keeps the work safe: everything inside the devcontainer, exact versions checked against their sums, no secrets and no learners' data in the repository. The packages, the recipes and the checks are in section 3.2 of docs/architecture.md, in Russian. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor#readme
documentation_interface_justification: tutor's external interface is the Go API of its public packages and the command line of its eval runner. Every exported identifier of the public packages, tutor, provider and the adapters provider/claude and provider/gpt, has a Go doc comment, 26 of 26 on 2026-11-01 (https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/provider/doc.go). `tutor-eval` run without arguments prints its commands with their flags, each command's -h describes every flag with its default, and the README walks through the commands (https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/cmd/tutor-eval/main.go). What the library is to become, call by call, is in sections 3.5 to 3.10 of docs/architecture.md, in Russian.
sites_https_justification: The project's site is its GitHub repository, served over HTTPS, and Go code takes the module over HTTPS too, through the Go module proxy: https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, open to anyone with a GitHub account, and nothing to install. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/issues
english_justification: The README, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, the code, its comments and the prompts are in English, and issues and pull requests are accepted in English or Russian. The documents under docs/ and the work plan, RUN.md, are in Russian, the author's working language.
maintained_justification: Under active development: 104 pull requests merged since the repository was created on 2026-10-19, the latest on 2026-11-01. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/commits/main
repo_public_justification: A public git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor
repo_track_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, and every commit of a pull request is signed off under the DCO, which a required check verifies.
repo_interim_justification: Every pull request, its branch and its commits are public before they reach main.
repo_distributed_justification: The repository is git, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version vX.Y.Z, tagged on its commit by .github's shared release workflow, which numbers it; the project's rule is that no tag is made by hand. Releases are immutable, a ruleset forbids moving or deleting a v* tag once it is made, and the Go module proxy and its checksum database hold each version of the Go module to its bytes. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
version_semver_justification: Versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, as Go modules take them: each release is the next patch of the current line, 0.1, starting at v0.1.0, and a new line is a change of RELEASE_LINE in the release workflow.
version_tags_justification: Each release is the git tag vX.Y.Z, which the release workflow creates together with the release, and the tag is also the Go module's version.
release_notes_justification: A release follows every merge to main that changes what the Go module is built from, and its notes on GitHub list the pull requests it brings, linked to each pull request's description: an English summary of what changed and why. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability of tutor has been fixed in any release. If one is, its release notes will name it and link its GitHub security advisory.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported as GitHub issues: https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/issues
report_tracker_justification: GitHub issues track individual reports. The project's own planned work is in its work plan, RUN.md.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been submitted yet (2026-11-01); the maintainer answers each report in its issue.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been submitted yet (2026-11-01); the maintainer answers each request in its issue.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public, permanent and searchable: https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The security policy, which every repository of the organization shares, says how to report a vulnerability: privately, through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting. It also says that the maintainer gives a first response within 14 days. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/security/policy
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled for tutor: a report goes over HTTPS to the maintainers and opens a draft advisory that only they and the reporter see. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in the last six months: tutor has no security advisory, draft or published (2026-11-01).
build_justification: tutor is Go. `just build` runs `go build ./...`, which builds every package from source, the eval runner tutor-eval among them, and `go run ./cmd/tutor-eval` builds and starts the runner. The Go is pinned: Go 1.27.3 in the toolchain stage of .devcontainer/Dockerfile, from an archive checked against its SHA-256, with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, and go.sum holds the hash of every module the build takes. CI builds that stage from a base image pinned by digest on every run and compiles every package in its checks: the tests, the linters and CodeQL's build of the Go code. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/justfile
build_common_tools_justification: The go command builds, vets and tests the code, with golangci-lint, govulncheck and go-licenses beside it; Docker builds the environment; and just runs every recipe.
build_floss_tools_justification: All FLOSS: Go (BSD-3-Clause), golangci-lint (GPL-3.0, a development tool that ships nothing), govulncheck (BSD-3-Clause), go-licenses (Apache-2.0), Docker Engine (Apache-2.0), Node.js (MIT), which runs the documents check, and just (CC0-1.0).
test_justification: tutor's automated test suite is the go command's own, `go test`, over 89 test files beside the code they test, in this repository under Apache-2.0. The tests run on synthetic strokes and sheets that the code draws and call no AI model: the adapters are tested against a local fake server. `just test` runs them, and `just ci-test` runs them with the race detector and without the test cache, as the required check Go / test does on every pull request and on main: https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: `go test ./...`, the standard way for Go, runs every test. `just test` runs it, `just ci-test` runs it with the race detector, as CI does, and `just --list` names the recipes.
test_most_justification: On 2026-11-06 the tests covered 95.2% of the statements of the module, as `go test -coverprofile` measures them. Every package is at 86% or more except the provider port, provider, at 54%. CI sends the coverage of each pull request and each commit to main to Codecov, and its check codecov/patch asks for 90% of new and changed lines: https://codecov.io/gh/altnovatrail/tutor
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs every check and every test on each pull request and on each commit to main. main takes a pull request only when they pass and its branch is up to date with main. https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: RULES.md, the rules every NovaTrail repository shares, which this repository's CLAUDE.md imports, says that code comes with its tests: a pull request that adds or changes what code does adds or changes the tests of its automated suite too. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/v0.9.4/RULES.md
tests_are_added_justification: The latest major changes came with their tests: the essays assessed in two calls, with tests of the call, its report and its command (https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/pull/101); the assessment by the rubric (#91); and the leak check of every hint, with tests that run spec's 17 leak vectors (#83).
tests_documented_added_justification: The rule on tests is in RULES.md, which the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md names as the rules every contribution follows. The checklist of the pull request template asks that code come with its tests: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
warnings_justification: golangci-lint runs its standard set (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck and unused) with errorlint, misspell, nolintlint and unconvert, and checks gofmt and goimports formatting. `just lint` runs it, and CI runs it as the required check Go / lint (https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/.golangci.yml). The recipes run bash with `set -euo pipefail`. SonarCloud analyses the code on every pull request, and its quality gate is a required check: https://sonarcloud.io/summary/new_code?id=altnovatrail_tutor
warnings_fixed_justification: On 2026-11-01 golangci-lint reports 0 issues, the code has no //nolint, and SonarCloud shows no open issue. A finding of SonarCloud or CodeQL is fixed in code before the next task starts; marking one false is a last resort, with the reason written down. https://sonarcloud.io/project/issues?id=altnovatrail_tutor
warnings_strict_justification: Go / lint fails on any finding of the linters, and nolintlint reports a //nolint that suppresses nothing. SonarCloud's quality gate holds a merge on any new bug or vulnerability, and the answer to a finding is a change to the code.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designs for least privilege, fail-safe defaults and a small attack surface. Every workflow starts with a read-only token, and a job gets only the write it needs: CodeQL and Scorecard to upload their results, and Scorecard an OIDC token to publish them; the workflows hold no secret. The branch main has no bypass, and a merge waits for the secret scan, the DCO sign-off, the documents check, the four Go checks, CodeQL's analyses of the Go code and of the workflows, and SonarCloud. The library's request types have no fields for a learner's or an account's identifiers, each AI provider's SDK is imported by its adapter alone, and tutor gives the platform no verdict: a program decides each one from what tutor reads. The check board serves only a loopback address, turns away a request whose Host is not local or whose Origin is another site, and writes the author's handwriting readable by its owner alone. A paid eval run starts only after its estimate and a typed yes, and starts no call that could take it past its dollar cap. The decisions behind these, in Russian, are in https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/main/docs/decisions.md
know_common_errors_justification: For this kind of software, a library and a command-line tool that send a learner's work to AI providers, with a local web page for the author, the maintainer counters: instructions hidden in the work for the model (on the platform a program, not the model, decides every verdict, the model's answer must follow a JSON schema and is decoded with unknown fields refused, and the runner checks every hint for the answer with the leak check); cross-site requests and DNS rebinding against the local board (it checks Host and Origin); writes in the wrong place (the board refuses any folder of the work tree outside samples/ and writes each sheet and picture as a new file, never over an older one); regular expressions that could backtrack on a long text (the leak check scans in loops); keys in the shell's history (the recipes ask for them without echo); script injection and untrusted checkouts in workflows (none, and Scorecard's Dangerous-Workflow check scores 10); and supply-chain tampering (actions and shared workflows pinned by commit, downloads checked against SHA-256 sums pinned in the Dockerfile, Go modules held by go.sum).
crypto_published_justification: tutor implements no cryptography. It relies on published and reviewed algorithms and protocols: TLS, through Go's crypto/tls, for every call to the AI providers, which the official SDKs make over HTTPS (https://api.anthropic.com and https://api.openai.com by default); and SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), which names the version of each prompt in a run's log, places each eval sheet in the split of a seed and names, by its digest, each bank of tasks whose open views a release carries. The Dockerfile of the devcontainer, which CI builds too, checks every archive it downloads against a SHA-256 sum pinned in the file.
crypto_call_justification: It calls Go's standard library (crypto/sha256, crypto/rand and, through net/http, crypto/tls) and sha256sum, and never implements cryptography itself.
crypto_floss_justification: Go's standard library is under BSD-3-Clause and sha256sum is part of GNU coreutils, and the SDKs that make the HTTPS calls are under MIT (anthropic-sdk-go) and Apache-2.0 (openai-go): all FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: tutor has no keys of its own and sets no key length: its HTTPS connections take the defaults of Go's crypto/tls. An API key for eval is a token the provider issues, not a cryptographic key.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is used: tutor's code calls SHA-256 alone, never MD5, SHA-1, DES or RC4, and sets no TLS option of its own, so its HTTPS connections take Go's crypto/tls defaults.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No algorithm with known serious weaknesses is used: SHA-256 only, never SHA-1 or MD5, and no TLS configuration of tutor's own.
crypto_pfs_justification: tutor implements no key agreement; its HTTPS connections are Go's crypto/tls.
crypto_password_storage_justification: tutor stores no passwords: it authenticates no users, and the board, which serves only this machine, has no sign-in. The eval API keys are credentials for the providers, which the criterion does not cover; they reach the process in environment variables, and the repository holds none.
crypto_random_justification: tutor generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; those of TLS are Go's crypto/tls. The board takes a random tail for a file name from crypto/rand, and math/rand/v2 only draws synthetic eval samples from a seed, so that the same seed draws the same sheets.
delivery_mitm_justification: tutor is delivered over HTTPS only: its repository, its releases and their files, and its Go module, which the go command fetches through the Go module proxy and checks against the checksum database, which holds each version to its bytes. Releases are immutable, GitHub attests each one with its files, which `gh release verify` and `gh release verify-asset` check, and each file is signed with cosign, its Sigstore bundle beside it in the release.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP. Every SHA-256 sum of an archive the devcontainer downloads is pinned in .devcontainer/Dockerfile next to its version, and the curl that fetches them is restricted to HTTPS, redirects included (--proto =https --proto-redir =https). The go command checks the Go modules against go.sum and the checksum database, over HTTPS. A release's SHA256SUMS comes signed, with its Sigstore bundle, in the same release as the files it sums.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability is open. Dependabot has raised no alert for tutor, govulncheck, a required check, found no vulnerability in the code tutor reaches on 2026-11-01, and neither CodeQL nor SonarCloud has an open finding. Scorecard's Vulnerabilities check scores 10.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Dependabot security updates are on, govulncheck runs on every pull request and on main as a required check, and a finding of SonarCloud or CodeQL is fixed in code before the next task starts.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the whole history on every pull request and on main (Secrets / gitleaks, a required check), and GitHub's secret scanning and push protection are on. The workflows hold no secret, and the keys for eval stay outside the repository: a run gets them in its environment.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, with the security-extended queries, analyses the Go code and every workflow, and SonarCloud analyses the repository, the board's HTML pages and their scripts among them, on every pull request and on main. golangci-lint runs staticcheck, go vet and the other linters of `just lint` (Go / lint), and govulncheck checks the code against the Go vulnerability database (Go / vuln). All of them are required checks of main's ruleset, CodeQL for each of its languages.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-extended queries and SonarCloud's security rules look for common vulnerabilities, and govulncheck for the known vulnerabilities of the Go vulnerability database in the Go code and the standard library it reaches (Go / vuln, a required check). SonarCloud found, and the pull request fixed before it merged, a Go tool installed in the Dockerfile without a lock file (docker:S8545, https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/pull/13). On main it found an npm install that would have run the packages' install scripts (docker:S6505), fixed on 2026-10-20.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The ruleset of main holds a merge on any CodeQL alert at error level or of high severity and above, and on SonarCloud's quality gate. CodeQL has raised no alert in tutor, and SonarCloud shows no open issue (2026-11-01): https://sonarcloud.io/project/issues?id=altnovatrail_tutor
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and on every commit to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The automated test suite runs on every pull request and on main with Go's race detector (`go test -race`, the required check Go / test), which watches the code for data races as it runs. Some tests vary their inputs: they run the generators of eval sheets over as many as 200 seeds and check every result against its rules. On 2026-11-01 the suite covered 95.1% of the statements; Go measures statements, not branches, and there is no fuzz test yet.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: tutor is written in Go, a memory-safe language, without cgo or the unsafe package; the board's pages run their scripts in the browser.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Go has no assert statement. The tests check their expectations with the testing package's t.Error and t.Fatal and run with the race detector, which CI turns on for the tests. The code checks what it reads, the files of samples, banks and plans and the models' answers, decoded with unknown fields refused, and returns an error.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: A failing test fails a required check, Go / test, and the pull request cannot merge until it passes. No vulnerability has been found this way.
